hook.text: Waves don't only exist on the surface—enormous waves travel along density layers deep inside the ocean.

buildup.text: Internal waves form at the boundary between water masses of different densities—like an underwater surface.

discovery.text: These hidden waves can be 100 meters tall—far larger than any surface wave.

twist.text: Internal waves move slowly because the density contrast between layers is tiny compared to air-water.

climax.text: They mix nutrients upward and affect submarine navigation—invisible but powerful.

punchline.text: The ocean's biggest waves are hidden—inside it.

quiz.question: Where do internal waves travel?
options: Along density boundaries inside the ocean
In the atmosphere above the ocean
